scope_line: Scope: the Agent Canvas (OpenHands repository), the software-agent-sdk that runs agents, and the Automation Service (OpenHands/automation) that schedules and dispatches automations. OpenHands Cloud operations are out of scope.

MAL-01.rationale: Agent runtime: generic business-object criterion (fixed per-archetype rule).

MAL-02.rationale: Agent runtime: generic business-object criterion (fixed per-archetype rule).

MAL-03.rationale: Agent runtime: generic business-object criterion (fixed per-archetype rule).

MAL-04.rationale: Agent runtime: generic CRUD criterion (fixed per-archetype rule).

MAL-05.rationale: Agent runtime: generic CRUD criterion (fixed per-archetype rule).

MAL-06.evidence: Typed client for the Agent Server API (src/api/open-hands.types.ts); the contract itself belongs to the Agent Server.

MAL-07.evidence: Canvas extensions are specified to contribute routed pages, panels, renderers, slots and themes as installable packages (specs/canvas-extensions.md), partly shipped behind capability detection; core layout is code.
MAL-07.alt_note: Once shipped, extensions are validated, installable layout data.

MAL-08.rationale: Agent runtime: generic CRUD views (fixed per-archetype rule).

MAL-09.evidence: Colour themes are palette definitions covering interface, code and terminal (src/themes/README.md); eight locale files.

MAL-10.evidence: Automations with cron and event triggers, templates and git sync are defined in the UI (src/types/automation.ts:3-13, src/routes/automation-*.tsx); they run on a separate automation server.

MAL-11.evidence: The agent server posts events to configured webhooks with buffering and retries (openhands-agent-server/openhands/agent_server/config.py:73-104).

MAL-12.evidence: Hooks run at defined points (openhands-sdk/openhands/sdk/hooks); agent actions run in Docker, Apptainer, cloud or remote workspaces (openhands-workspace/openhands/workspace), but hook isolation and egress control were not verified.
MAL-12.alt_note: If hooks execute inside the sandboxed workspace.

GOV-01.evidence: Component library with accessibility lint rules (eslint.config.js); no automated accessibility scans. Scored at the lower reading under rule 11 because: If lint rules without scans count as no automation.
GOV-01.alt_note: The September v0.3 pass scored 2 on the evidence above.

GOV-02.evidence: No audit store in the canvas; durable audit is documented only through an external DefenseClaw integration (docs/DefenseClaw.md).

GOV-03.evidence: Telemetry is consent-gated with opt-out (src/services/telemetry.ts:9-29); there is no data export or erasure feature in the canvas.
GOV-03.alt_note: Consent management is a privacy control, though not export or erasure.

GOV-04.evidence: No security scanning in CI; runtime security is delegated to the Agent Server or external guardrails (docs/DefenseClaw.md).

GOV-05.evidence: Automation definitions sync to git (src/routes/automation-git-sync.tsx); other settings are unversioned.

GOV-07.evidence: Confirmation policies (never, always, confirm risky) decide which agent actions need a person (openhands-sdk/openhands/sdk/security/confirmation_policy.py:27-43); they govern actions, not changes to the agent itself.

GOV-08.evidence: CI checks REST API breakage, persisted-settings compatibility and deprecations on every change (software-agent-sdk .github/workflows/agent-server-rest-api-breakage.yml, persisted-settings-compat.yml, deprecation-check.yml).

ARC-01.rationale: Agent runtime: generic-store query performance (fixed per-archetype rule).

ARC-05.evidence: Single user by default, with a Helm chart for team deployments (helm/agent-canvas).

ARC-06.evidence: No performance suite or documented limits (searched for benchmark, load test and perf).

DEL-02.evidence: The canvas deploys separately from the Agent Server and Automation Server behind an API contract, as an npm library, desktop app, container and Helm chart (docs/architecture.md, electron/, docker/, helm/).

DEL-03.evidence: Library entrypoints and lint configuration; no architectural boundary tests.

DEL-05.evidence: Lint, unit tests and builds on Ubuntu and Windows plus mocked-LLM Playwright E2E on pull requests (.github/workflows/ci.yml:4-66, mock-llm-e2e.yml); mutation testing (stryker.config.mjs); no accessibility or security checks.
DEL-05.alt_note: Coverage is broad, including mutation testing.

MAL-13.evidence: Skills, plugins and MCP servers are configured through the canvas (src/routes/skills-plugins.tsx, mcp-settings.tsx); canvas extensions for UI are partly shipped.
MAL-13.alt_note: Once extensions ship, UI, layout and theme are all plugin points.

MAL-14.evidence: No isolation model for canvas extensions is evidenced; agent code isolation is delegated to backends.

MAL-15.evidence: Mocked-LLM development server and seed scripts (scripts/seed-automation-ux-data.mjs, docs/DEVELOPMENT.md).

MAL-19.evidence: The canvas consumes MCP and exposes a UI tool that lets agents drive the canvas (tools/canvas_ui_tool.py); no MCP server for the canvas itself.

ai.evidence: A UI tool lets agents drive the canvas; no MCP server for it.

MAL-20.evidence: Users run agent conversations with actions through the canvas; there is no natural-language authoring of canvas definitions.

ai.evidence: Model-backed agent conversations through the canvas.

GOV-09.evidence: The default confirmation policy is NeverConfirm (openhands-sdk/openhands/sdk/conversation/state.py:123); with ConfirmRisky, LLM security analyzers classify each action's risk and risky ones pause for a person (security/llm_analyzer.py, toolshield_llm_analyzer.py, ensemble.py).

ai.evidence: Confirmation policy defaults to never; with ConfirmRisky, an LLM security analyser classifies actions (openhands-sdk/openhands/sdk/conversation/state.py:123).

MAL-16.evidence: OpenHands, Claude Code, Codex, Gemini and other ACP agents map onto one agent protocol, so adding an agent is configuration (docs/ACP_AGENTS.md).

MAL-17.evidence: Backends (local, Docker, VM, cloud) and ACP agents are configurable; no connector SDK with lifecycle.
MAL-17.alt_note: ACP is a standard connector definition.

MAL-18.evidence: Relies on the versioned Agent Server API and ACP; no deprecation windows in the canvas.

EXP-01.evidence: Kernel of conversations, backends, automations, profiles and skills with no business-domain nouns; channels exist only as automation outputs.

EXP-02.evidence: Automation templates cover new tasks without kernel change (src/routes/automation-templates.tsx).

EXP-03.evidence: Automation templates and git sync; installable canvas extensions are partly shipped.

LRN-01.evidence: Consent-gated product analytics to PostHog (src/services/telemetry.ts); not available to product features.

LRN-02.evidence: No typed feedback or learning signals in the canvas or the SDK.

LRN-04.evidence: No joined mining in the canvas.

LRN-06.evidence: No proposals for changing the canvas.

ai.evidence: No AI involvement in this behaviour.

DEL-04.evidence: Automations run coding agents on users' repositories (automation repository README); nothing implements changes to OpenHands' own definitions. Recorded under the self rule.
DEL-04.alt_note: Automations configured in OpenHands are operator-configured behaviour run by an AI lane.

ai.evidence: Automations change users' repositories, not OpenHands itself.

LRN-09.evidence: Plugin automations tag each run with its experiment and variant (openhands/automation/presets/plugin/sdk_main.py:514-530), so variants can be compared by hand; nothing records a baseline or decision.
LRN-09.alt_note: Variant-tagged runs are telemetry bound to the change.

DEL-06.evidence: Backend server_info with runtime services (docs/architecture.md) and container health in the entrypoint (docker/entrypoint.sh).

DEL-07.evidence: Docker, Helm and desktop builds; mocked-LLM Docker E2E stands up an environment per run (.github/workflows/mock-llm-docker-e2e.yml).

DEL-08.evidence: Playwright journeys with mocked and live configurations and a testing matrix (docs/TESTING_MATRIX.md); no changed-path map or adoption instrumentation.
DEL-08.alt_note: The testing matrix maps surfaces to journeys.

LRN-07.evidence: No learning from sessions was found in the SDK (searched openhands-sdk/openhands/sdk/skills, context, agent).

ai.evidence: No AI involvement in this behaviour.

LRN-08.evidence: Critics evaluate task output for iterative refinement (openhands-sdk/openhands/sdk/critic), not changes to the agent itself.

ARC-02.evidence: Alembic migrations with downgrade steps, and a test of the migration history (automation repository: migrations/versions, tests/test_migration_history.py); no enforced online strategy.
ARC-02.alt_note: Migration history is tested in CI.

ARC-03.evidence: The Automation Service is a stateless FastAPI app over PostgreSQL and object storage; the canvas ships a Helm chart (helm/agent-canvas).

ARC-04.evidence: A scheduler and watchdog drive runs with timeouts and terminal states (automation repository: openhands/automation/scheduler.py, watchdog.py); git sync backs off after failures (migrations/versions/029_add_git_sync_failure_backoff.py).
ARC-04.alt_note: Watchdog recovery and back-off approach level 3.

ARC-07.evidence: Telemetry for runs and the key-value store (openhands/automation/telemetry.py, kv_metrics.py); no objectives.

ARC-08.evidence: Each run executes in its own sandbox with timeouts and cleanup (openhands/automation/watchdog.py); repeatedly failing automations are disabled (migrations/versions/020_add_automation_disabled_reason.py).

ai.evidence: Fallback strategy on provider errors, tested (tests/sdk/llm/test_llm_fallback.py).

ARC-09.evidence: No backup command or documented backup for the Automation Service database or storage.

DEL-01.evidence: No request or feature-request object for changing the product was found; requests live outside it.

ai.evidence: No AI involvement in this behaviour.

DEL-09.evidence: Plugin automations can split runs between weighted variants (openhands/automation/presets/plugin/sdk_main.py:349-373).

DEL-10.evidence: Automations can be disabled at runtime, and unhealthy ones are disabled automatically (tests/test_unhealthy_automations.py).

LRN-03.evidence: Runs record failure kinds and status details, and unhealthy automations are detected (openhands/automation/watchdog.py, migrations/versions/016_add_run_status_detail.py).

LRN-05.evidence: Failed runs keep their phase, failure kind and conversation for inspection (docs/run-phase-reporting.md).

EXP-04.evidence: No record of unmet intents was found.

ai.evidence: No AI involvement in this behaviour.

EXP-06.evidence: Presets and plugins are available to every organisation.

DEL-11.rationale: Scope fact code_release_path is false: Automations act on users' repositories; no first-party lane ships OpenHands code changes.

AIR-01.evidence: LLM fallback strategy on connection, rate-limit and server errors, plus routers (openhands-sdk/openhands/sdk/llm/fallback_strategy.py, router), with tests (tests/sdk/llm/test_llm_fallback.py).

AIR-02.evidence: Conversation cost and budget-exceeded handling (fallback_strategy.py), and run cost recorded per automation (automation repository: migrations/versions/013_add_run_cost.py); no per-user budgets.

AIR-03.evidence: Agents work in a sandboxed workspace with repository files, skills and microagents loaded automatically.

AIR-04.evidence: Each conversation runs in its own sandbox with the user's provider tokens; automations use per-user API keys (automation repository: openhands/automation/auth.py), with tests.

AIR-05.evidence: Behaviour and integration test suites for agents (tests/integration) and SWE-bench evaluation runs (.github/workflows/run-eval.yml).

AIR-06.evidence: Integration tests and evaluations run on labelled pull requests and releases (.github/workflows/integration-runner.yml, run-eval.yml); not blocking by default.

AIR-07.evidence: The event stream persists every action, observation and tool call per conversation, with LLM call metadata (openhands-sdk/openhands/sdk/conversation).

AIR-08.evidence: Critics score task output during a run; no production quality monitoring.

limits: Repository evidence only. The Automation Service was added for v0.4 after the inter-rater study found it missing; it is beta. No live runs. Single rater.
reading: **SAL 1.** With the Automation Service now in scope, OpenHands has a hosted, multi-organisation architecture, but no load suite (ARC-06 0) or backup (ARC-09 0), which caps the foundation at L1. Automations run coding agents on users' repositories, which the self rule excludes (DEL-04 1). Runs record failure kinds and unhealthy automations are disabled automatically (LRN-03 2, DEL-10 2). **Next level:** backup and capacity evidence for the Automation Service, and a lane that improves OpenHands' own skills and automations.

persistent_data.evidence: The Automation Service keeps automations, runs and a key-value store in PostgreSQL (automation repository, migrations/versions).

schema_changes.evidence: Alembic migrations in the Automation Service (migrations/versions, 29 files).

multi_tenant.evidence: The Automation Service serves organisations with org-scoped data (migrations/versions/023_org_scoped_git_sync.py).

hosted_service.evidence: The Automation Service and Agent Server run as long-lived services for OpenHands Cloud.

machine_actions.evidence: The Agent Server and Automation Service APIs create and run automations with per-user API keys (automation repository: openhands/automation/auth.py).

agent_mutations.evidence: Agents change users' repositories, not OpenHands' own definitions.

evolution_auto_apply.evidence: Nothing changes OpenHands' own definitions automatically.

definition_change_path.evidence: Automations, skills and settings are definitions.

code_release_path.evidence: Automations act on users' repositories; no first-party lane ships OpenHands code changes.

ai_data_access.evidence: Agents read repositories and workspace files in their sandbox.

ai_actions.evidence: Agents edit code, run commands and open pull requests; automations run them unattended.
